newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's star criminal dies in prison attack.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's star criminal dies in prison attack.

text.p: Brazil's most famous convict, renowned for giving on-the-run interviews and mocking police attempts to catch him, was killed by fellow inmates on Monday, prison officials said.

Leonardo Pareja, 22, and two other inmates died from gunshot and stab wounds after being attacked by five prisoners in what appeared to be a flare-up in a long-running battle for power within the jail, prison spokesman Valdir Morgado said.

He said officials also believed last week's discovery of a tunnel being dug by inmates might have sparked the fighting at the Agroindustrial Penitentiary in the central city of Goiania, 120 miles (200 km) southwest of capital Brasilia.
"We have information that Pareja was in charge of the escape attempt. His girlfriend has been telling reporters that he planned to meet her in time for New Year's Eve," Morgado said.

Police and prison officials were questioning the five men who were involved in the attack and a prison officer has been arrested on suspicion of providing the gang with a revolver they used, the spokesman said.

Pareja became a household name in Brazil last year when, already a convicted armed robber and on the run, he took a girl hostage to escape police and went on a 40-day spree of hold-ups and high-speed chases in Brazil's backlands. He mocked police in telephone interviews with radio and television stations before giving himself up.

In April, he reappeared as a ringleader of a six-day prison rebellion that ended in a mass escape. Again, Pareja surrendered, but only after reportedly buying a round of drinks in a bar, kissing female fans and signing autographs.

The escapade ended in bloodshed when two other fugitives were killed by police and a student died when he was caught in crossfire. Before Monday's killings, four men involved in the rebellion had been killed and news reports said Pareja believed his life was at risk in jail.

Brazilians followed every step of Pareja's spectacular criminal career with a fascination usually reserved for the private lives of soap opera actors and soccer stars. In May, lawyers representing him signed a deal for a full-length feature film on his life story.

The killing dominated Brazil's media on Monday. "Exhibitionist, intelligent, cruel, bon viveur, cold, audacious -- Leonardo Pareja was a different kind of criminal," intoned a television news anchor on national Globo Network. "For him, speaking to the cameras was as easy as committing a crime."
